subject: Nanotechnology
title: Templates and Directed Assembly
description: A micro-lesson that makes Templates and Directed Assembly usable.

hook.text: Pure self-assembly is random in orientation — templates add a guide rail, directing where structures form.

buildup.text: Patterned surfaces, electric fields, and flow channels all serve as templates — guiding assembly without touching parts.

discovery.text: Directed self-assembly combines top-down lithography with bottom-up chemistry — the best of both worlds.

twist.text: Semiconductor companies use DSA for sub-10 nm chip features — self-assembly makes what lithography alone cannot.

climax.text: Block copolymers on patterned guides self-organize into perfect lines and dots — nanoscale order from simple chemistry.

punchline.text: Give self-assembly a hint and it builds with nanometer precision.

quiz.question: What is directed self-assembly (DSA)?
options: Using robots to place individual atoms on a surface
Combining top-down templates with bottom-up self-assembly to guide nanoscale structure formation
Allowing components to assemble completely randomly without any guidance
